examples.scenario: Pixel centre lies exactly on parcel exterior ring and code uses ST_Contains.
examples.reason: Contains excludes boundary-only points while Covers includes them.

examples.scenario: Pixel centre lies exactly on parcel exterior ring and membership policy changes between runs.
examples.reason: Boundary inclusion must be serialized before sampling.

examples.scenario: A polygon self-intersects but point-in-polygon is executed anyway.
examples.reason: GDAL/PostGIS warn invalid geometries can produce incorrect predicate results.

examples.scenario: Only a boolean invalid flag is stored, with no reason/location.
examples.reason: Reason and error location make topology failures auditable.

examples.scenario: A hole lies outside its shell and membership is evaluated.
examples.reason: Hole-outside-shell is invalid Simple Features geometry.

examples.scenario: Nested shells are accepted as a valid MultiPolygon.
examples.reason: Nested shells can violate polygon validity rules.

examples.scenario: MakeValid silently changes one polygon into multiple polygons.
examples.reason: Repair output can change geometry type/structure.

examples.scenario: Linework and structure repair algorithms return different area coverage.
examples.reason: Make-valid algorithm choice is a numeric membership dependency.

examples.scenario: Repaired geometry replaces authoritative boundary bytes without retaining original.
examples.reason: Repair is derived processing, not authoritative provenance.

examples.scenario: SetPrecision grid size changes between runs.
examples.reason: Topology and vertex coordinates may change with precision model.

examples.scenario: Pointwise precision rounding is used for terminal polygon membership.
examples.reason: Pointwise reduction can create invalid polygon topology.

examples.scenario: SnapToGrid collapses adjacent vertices but collapse count is ignored.
examples.reason: Grid snapping can remove points and alter geometry simplicity.

examples.scenario: Area changes after precision reduction but membership proceeds silently.
examples.reason: Area drift signals a changed parcel representation.

examples.scenario: Perimeter changes after precision reduction but no threshold/policy exists.
examples.reason: Boundary length drift is part of geometry mutation provenance.

examples.scenario: Vertex count changes after make-valid and output is treated as equivalent.
examples.reason: Topology repair can restructure rings even when visually similar.

examples.scenario: A pixel lies on an interior-hole boundary and code treats holes like exterior rings implicitly.
examples.reason: Interior-ring boundary semantics must be explicit.

examples.scenario: A pixel lies strictly inside a parcel hole and is included.
examples.reason: Hole interiors are exterior to the polygon surface.

examples.scenario: ST_Intersects is used as a substitute for parcel-cell membership.
examples.reason: Intersects only requires any shared point and is broader than chosen centre-based membership.

examples.scenario: A pixel-centre DE-9IM relation changes but boolean result happens to stay true.
examples.reason: Exact topological relation is stronger replay evidence than one boolean.

examples.scenario: Boundary geometry CRS label matches but WKB differs.
examples.reason: Same CRS does not prove same parcel geometry bytes.

examples.scenario: Boundary WKB matches but CRS WKT differs.
examples.reason: Coordinate values require the same spatial-reference interpretation.

examples.scenario: Coverage has a narrow gap between adjacent authoritative polygons.
examples.reason: Coverage validity is separate from individual polygon validity.

examples.scenario: Adjacent parcel polygons overlap and both claim the same pixel centre.
examples.reason: Overlapping coverage creates ambiguous ownership.

examples.scenario: Shared boundary edges have mismatched node locations.
examples.reason: Valid coverage requires compatible shared-edge noding.

examples.scenario: Coverage-clean tool modifies source boundaries to remove overlap.
examples.reason: Coverage cleaning is an explicit mutating repair operation.

examples.scenario: A tiny sliver is individually valid and therefore assumed authoritative.
examples.reason: GDAL notes qualitative spikes/slivers are outside validity testing.

examples.scenario: Curved geometry is linearized differently across environments before validation.
examples.reason: Linearization can change validity and membership near boundaries.

examples.scenario: Z coordinates separate overlapping polygons but 2D validity passes them as distinct.
examples.reason: GEOS validity is fundamentally 2D for these operations.

examples.scenario: Ring orientation alone is used to decide shell versus hole validity.
examples.reason: GEOS does not require a particular ring orientation for validity.

examples.scenario: Repeated points in a ring are treated as automatic invalidity.
examples.reason: GEOS permits repeated ring points in validity checks.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent boundary WKB digests differ but areas match.
examples.reason: Equal area does not prove identical parcel topology.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent WKB match but membership bitmaps differ.
examples.reason: Same geometry must produce the same chosen membership result.

examples.scenario: Membership bitmap matches but DE-9IM boundary-touch ledger differs.
examples.reason: Boundary-only cases must remain explainable even if final bitmap matches.

examples.scenario: Boundary-touch pixels are nudged inward by epsilon before testing.
examples.reason: Artificial coordinate movement changes the membership question.

examples.scenario: A bbox prefilter is accepted as final polygon membership.
examples.reason: Bounding-box overlap is only an optimization, not exact topology.

examples.scenario: Static topology QA completes while exact boundary rows remain zero.
examples.reason: Guards can advance without fabricating authoritative parcel geometry.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second geometry runner is launched while shared runner ACK is absent.
examples.reason: Continuation contract requires the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: A repaired example boundary is reported as the actual target parcel boundary.
examples.reason: Examples are QA fixtures, not target authoritative geometry.

examples.scenario: Batch 77 is reported as measured parcel height output.
examples.reason: Real height still requires canonical target, authoritative exact boundary, raster binding and runtime sampling.
